title: Check for major economic news
description: Check today's economic calendar for high-impact events that could cause significant volatility.
advice: Focus on interest-rate decisions, CPI, employment reports, GDP, PCE, central-bank events, and other high-impact releases.

title: Check whether news affects my pair
description: Identify whether upcoming economic events directly affect either currency in your trading pair.
advice: For EUR/USD, pay close attention to major EUR and USD events. For GBP/JPY, focus on GBP and JPY events.

title: Check the timing of major news
description: Determine whether important news is scheduled before, during, or shortly after your planned trading window.
advice: Know exactly when the release happens before planning an entry. Avoid entering immediately before major releases unless your strategy specifically accounts for them.

title: Check Actual vs Forecast
description: Compare the released economic figure with the market's expected forecast.
advice: A significant difference between Actual and Forecast can create strong volatility. Observe price reaction instead of assuming the result automatically determines direction.

title: Check Previous vs Actual
description: Compare the latest economic reading with the previous reading to understand whether conditions are improving or deteriorating.
advice: Consider Previous, Forecast, and Actual together rather than relying on a single number.

title: Check the market reaction
description: Observe how price actually responds to economic news instead of relying only on the headline.
advice: Watch price action, volatility, momentum, and structure after the release. The reaction can differ from what the economic number appears to suggest.

title: Check DXY
description: Review the US Dollar Index when trading USD-related pairs.
advice: Use DXY to understand broader USD strength or weakness and compare its behavior with your USD pair.

title: Check Gold (XAU/USD)
description: Review Gold for additional context about USD behavior, risk sentiment, and safe-haven demand.
advice: Use Gold as supporting information rather than treating it as a standalone trading signal.

title: Check the current trading session
description: Identify which major forex session is currently active and how that may affect market activity.
advice: London and New York sessions generally provide more activity for many major pairs. Consider whether your chosen pair is normally active during the current session.

title: Check liquidity
description: Determine whether there is enough market participation for normal price movement and execution.
advice: Be cautious during unusually quiet periods, session transitions, holidays, or other conditions where liquidity may be reduced.

title: Check the spread
description: Review the current bid-ask spread before entering a trade.
advice: Compare the current spread with what is normal for your pair. Be cautious when spreads become unusually wide around news or low-liquidity periods.

title: Check for central-bank events
description: Identify upcoming interest-rate decisions, monetary-policy statements, press conferences, and major central-bank speeches.
advice: Central-bank events can produce large and prolonged moves. Treat them as high-risk macro events.

title: Check for major market holidays
description: Determine whether major financial centers are closed or operating with reduced activity.
advice: Expect potentially lower liquidity and different market behavior during major holidays.

title: Check for multiple major events
description: Look for several important economic releases occurring close together.
advice: A cluster of major events can create repeated volatility and make technical analysis less reliable.

title: Check the broader market environment
description: Determine whether the broader market environment appears to favor risk-taking or risk reduction.
advice: Look at broad market behavior and major assets for context, but avoid building your entire trade thesis around one macro indicator.

title: Check major geopolitical events
description: Look for wars, elections, political crises, sanctions, trade disputes, or other events that could rapidly affect currencies and risk sentiment.
advice: Be especially cautious when geopolitical developments are actively changing and market reactions are unpredictable.

title: Check bond yields
description: Review major government bond yields when they are relevant to your currency analysis.
advice: Changes in yields can provide useful context for interest-rate expectations and currency strength, especially for USD pairs.

title: Check risk sentiment
description: Determine whether markets currently appear to favor risk-on or risk-off behavior.
advice: Compare major equity indexes, currencies, and safe-haven assets to understand the broader risk environment.

title: Check volatility conditions
description: Determine whether the market is unusually calm or experiencing elevated volatility.
advice: High volatility can create larger candles and wider stops, while extremely low volatility can produce slow or choppy conditions.

title: Check for unexpected market shocks
description: Look for breaking news or sudden events that are not present on the normal economic calendar.
advice: If unexpected news causes abnormal price movement, pause and reassess instead of immediately entering based on the existing setup.

title: Check whether conditions are tradeable
description: Make a final assessment of whether the current macro environment is suitable for continuing your technical analysis.
advice: You do not need to trade every market condition. If news, liquidity, volatility, or uncertainty makes the environment unclear, waiting is a valid decision.

title: Identify the higher-timeframe direction
description: Determine whether the market is generally bullish, bearish, or ranging on the higher timeframes.
advice: Start with the Daily and 4H charts before moving to lower timeframes. Look at the overall direction rather than individual candles.

title: Determine bullish or bearish conditions
description: Decide whether buyers or sellers currently have greater control of the market.
advice: Look for consistent higher highs and higher lows for bullish conditions, or lower highs and lower lows for bearish conditions.

title: Check market structure
description: Use swing highs and swing lows to understand the current structural direction.
advice: Do not determine bias from one candle. Look at meaningful swing points and how price is developing between them.

title: Check the latest swing high
description: Identify the most important recent swing high and observe how price is behaving around it.
advice: A break and acceptance above a meaningful swing high can support bullish bias, while rejection can weaken it.

title: Check the latest swing low
description: Identify the most important recent swing low and observe how price is behaving around it.
advice: A break and acceptance below a meaningful swing low can support bearish bias, while strong rejection can weaken it.

title: Check for higher highs and higher lows
description: Determine whether price is creating a sequence of higher highs and higher lows.
advice: A consistent sequence supports bullish market structure, but wait for meaningful swings rather than minor market noise.

title: Check for lower highs and lower lows
description: Determine whether price is creating a sequence of lower highs and lower lows.
advice: A consistent sequence supports bearish market structure, but avoid labeling every small pullback as a new lower high.

title: Check for a ranging market
description: Determine whether price is moving sideways between clearly defined support and resistance areas.
advice: If neither buyers nor sellers are consistently controlling structure, classify the market as ranging instead of forcing a bullish or bearish bias.

title: Check for trend continuation
description: Determine whether the existing trend is still producing valid structure and momentum.
advice: Look for healthy pullbacks followed by continuation instead of assuming that every trend will continue indefinitely.

title: Check for possible trend reversal
description: Look for evidence that the current directional bias may be losing strength or changing.
advice: Watch for structural breaks, failed continuation, strong rejection, and changes in momentum before changing your bias.

title: Check for Break of Structure
description: Determine whether price has broken an important structural high or low.
advice: A meaningful break can provide evidence of continuation or a potential shift, but distinguish real structural breaks from short-lived liquidity grabs.

title: Check for Change of Character
description: Look for an early sign that market behavior may be shifting from the existing trend.
advice: Treat a change in behavior as an alert rather than automatic confirmation of a reversal.

title: Check higher-timeframe support
description: Determine whether price is approaching or reacting from an important higher-timeframe support area.
advice: Strong support can influence bearish setups and may create conditions for a bounce or reversal.

title: Check higher-timeframe resistance
description: Determine whether price is approaching or reacting from an important higher-timeframe resistance area.
advice: Strong resistance can influence bullish setups and may create conditions for rejection or reversal.

title: Check premium and discount
description: Determine whether current price is relatively high or low within a meaningful trading range.
advice: For a bullish idea, consider whether price is in a relatively favorable lower portion of the range. For bearish ideas, consider the upper portion.

title: Check moving-average direction
description: Use moving averages as supporting information for trend direction and momentum.
advice: Look at the slope and relationship of commonly used moving averages rather than using a crossover alone as your bias.

title: Check EMA alignment
description: Determine whether short-, medium-, and longer-term EMAs are aligned with the current directional move.
advice: Bullish alignment can support a bullish bias and bearish alignment can support a bearish bias, but use structure as the primary context.

title: Check momentum
description: Assess whether price is moving with strong directional momentum or losing momentum.
advice: Strong momentum can support continuation, while weakening momentum near important levels may warn of a possible reversal.

title: Check volume
description: Use volume to understand participation behind important price movements when reliable volume data is available.
advice: Compare volume around breakouts, reversals, and major levels rather than interpreting one volume spike in isolation.

title: Check DXY for USD pairs
description: Use the US Dollar Index as additional context when forming a bias on USD-related pairs.
advice: Compare DXY structure and momentum with your USD pair. Use it as confirmation rather than a standalone directional signal.

title: Check correlated markets
description: Review markets that may provide additional context for the instrument being analyzed.
advice: Look for meaningful relationships between your pair and related currencies, commodities, indices, or yields.

title: Check risk-on or risk-off conditions
description: Determine whether broader markets are currently favoring risk-taking or defensive behavior.
advice: Use major indices, safe-haven assets, and currency behavior to understand the broader environment.

title: Check the weekly direction
description: Review the weekly chart to understand the broader directional context.
advice: The weekly chart can help prevent lower-timeframe analysis from creating a misleading view of the overall market.

title: Check the daily direction
description: Use the Daily chart to establish the primary directional context for your trade.
advice: Identify the dominant structure, important levels, and current price location before moving to lower timeframes.

title: Check the 4H direction
description: Use the 4H chart to refine the higher-timeframe market bias.
advice: Look for whether the 4H structure agrees with or contradicts the Daily direction.

title: Compare multiple timeframes
description: Determine whether the major timeframes agree with each other or are showing conflicting signals.
advice: When timeframes disagree, recognize the conflict instead of forcing a single directional bias.

title: Check price location
description: Determine where current price sits relative to major highs, lows, support, resistance, and trading ranges.
advice: The same bullish or bearish pattern can have very different implications depending on where it occurs.

title: Check liquidity above price
description: Identify obvious highs and areas where buy-side liquidity may be concentrated.
advice: Use liquidity areas as potential targets or reaction zones rather than assuming price must move toward them.

title: Check liquidity below price
description: Identify obvious lows and areas where sell-side liquidity may be concentrated.
advice: Consider whether nearby lows could act as targets or reaction areas before deciding on directional bias.

title: Check for conflicting signals
description: Identify whether different indicators, timeframes, or market structures are giving contradictory information.
advice: When evidence conflicts, reduce confidence in the bias instead of adding more indicators until you get the answer you want.

title: Define bullish invalidation
description: Determine what price action would prove your bullish market bias wrong.
advice: Before looking for long entries, identify the structural level or condition that would invalidate the bullish thesis.

title: Define bearish invalidation
description: Determine what price action would prove your bearish market bias wrong.
advice: Before looking for short entries, identify the structural level or condition that would invalidate the bearish thesis.

title: Separate bias from entry
description: Recognize that having a bullish or bearish bias does not mean an entry is currently available.
advice: Use market bias to determine what direction you prefer, then wait for your separate entry-confirmation process.

title: Write the current bias
description: Clearly state your current market bias before continuing to the next stage of analysis.
advice: Write something specific such as Bullish, Bearish, or Neutral/Range, along with the main evidence supporting the decision.

title: Define the invalidation point
description: Record the exact condition that would force you to reconsider your current market bias.
advice: A good bias should have a clear reason and a clear condition under which you will abandon it.

title: Assign confidence to the bias
description: Evaluate how strongly the available evidence supports your current directional view.
advice: Use a simple confidence level such as Low, Medium, or High. Do not confuse high confidence with certainty.

title: Identify the current market structure
description: Determine whether the market is trending upward, trending downward, or moving sideways.
advice: Start with clear swing points. Avoid defining structure from small candles or random short-term movements.

title: Mark major swing highs
description: Identify the important highs that price has created on the current timeframe.
advice: Focus on significant turning points that caused meaningful price movement.

title: Mark major swing lows
description: Identify the important lows that price has created on the current timeframe.
advice: Prioritize lows that caused meaningful reactions or directional moves.

title: Check for Higher Highs
description: Determine whether price is creating new highs above previous significant highs.
advice: A sequence of higher highs supports bullish structure when confirmed by meaningful swing points.

title: Check for Higher Lows
description: Determine whether pullbacks are creating lows above previous significant lows.
advice: Higher lows show that buyers are defending increasingly higher prices.

title: Check for Lower Highs
description: Determine whether rallies are failing below previous significant highs.
advice: Lower highs can indicate that sellers are becoming increasingly active.

title: Check for Lower Lows
description: Determine whether price is creating new lows below previous significant lows.
advice: A sequence of lower lows supports bearish structure when the breaks are meaningful.

title: Identify the protected high
description: Find the high that should remain intact if the current bearish structure is still valid.
advice: A meaningful break above a protected high may weaken or invalidate the bearish structural thesis.

title: Identify the protected low
description: Find the low that should remain intact if the current bullish structure is still valid.
advice: A meaningful break below a protected low may weaken or invalidate the bullish structural thesis.

title: Check Break of Structure (BOS)
description: Determine whether price has broken a significant swing point in the direction of the existing trend.
advice: A BOS is more meaningful when the broken level is a clear structural swing rather than minor market noise.

title: Check Change of Character (CHOCH)
description: Look for a structural event that may indicate a transition from the current trend to a potential reversal.
advice: Treat CHOCH as an early warning rather than automatic confirmation of a complete trend reversal.

title: Check Market Structure Shift (MSS)
description: Look for a meaningful change in the sequence of highs and lows that suggests control may be changing.
advice: Look for displacement and a meaningful structural break rather than labeling every small reversal as an MSS.

title: Check internal structure
description: Analyze the smaller structural movements occurring inside the larger market structure.
advice: Internal structure can help refine entries, but do not allow minor movements to override major higher-timeframe structure without evidence.

title: Check external structure
description: Identify the larger swing structure controlling the broader market direction.
advice: External structure should generally carry more weight than minor internal movements when determining the primary trend.

title: Compare internal and external structure
description: Determine whether the lower-timeframe structure agrees with the larger market structure.
advice: A temporary countertrend move does not automatically mean the higher-timeframe trend has reversed.

title: Check impulse and correction
description: Separate strong directional movements from corrective price movements.
advice: Healthy trends often consist of impulsive moves followed by controlled corrections.

title: Check the strength of the impulse
description: Determine whether a structural move has strong momentum or weak movement.
advice: Large-bodied candles, strong displacement, and decisive movement can provide stronger structural evidence than slow overlapping candles.

title: Check for displacement
description: Look for a strong and decisive price movement that rapidly moves away from an area.
advice: Strong displacement can make a structural break more meaningful, especially when it breaks an important swing point.

title: Check for weak structure
description: Identify slow, overlapping, or indecisive price action that does not clearly establish direction.
advice: When structure is unclear, classify the market as uncertain instead of forcing a trend.

title: Check for consolidation
description: Determine whether price is compressing within a relatively narrow range.
advice: Consolidation often precedes expansion, but do not assume which direction the breakout will occur.

title: Mark the current trading range
description: Identify the meaningful high and low defining the current range.
advice: Use the range to understand where price is located and whether it is near the upper or lower boundary.

title: Check range expansion
description: Determine whether price has broken out of the established trading range with meaningful momentum.
advice: Look for acceptance and follow-through rather than assuming every temporary break is a genuine breakout.

title: Check failed breakouts
description: Identify situations where price breaks a structural level but quickly returns inside the previous range.
advice: A failed breakout can provide important information about rejection and trapped traders.

title: Check liquidity sweeps
description: Identify when price moves through an obvious high or low before reversing back into the previous structure.
advice: A liquidity sweep alone is not confirmation of reversal. Wait for subsequent structural evidence.

title: Check equal highs
description: Identify multiple highs forming around a similar price level.
advice: Equal highs can become an obvious liquidity area and may be important when evaluating future price movement.

title: Check equal lows
description: Identify multiple lows forming around a similar price level.
advice: Equal lows can become an obvious liquidity area and may be important when evaluating future price movement.

title: Check multi-timeframe structure
description: Compare structure across higher and lower timeframes.
advice: Use higher timeframes to understand the dominant structure and lower timeframes to refine the current movement.

title: Check structure around key levels
description: Observe how price behaves when approaching important support, resistance, supply, demand, or other key areas.
advice: Structural changes near important levels can be more meaningful than the same movement occurring in the middle of nowhere.

title: Check whether structure supports the bias
description: Compare the current structural evidence with the directional bias established in the previous step.
advice: If structure contradicts your existing bias, reassess the bias instead of forcing the chart to match your original idea.

title: Define structural invalidation
description: Identify the price level or structural event that would invalidate your current structural interpretation.
advice: Know exactly what would make your bullish, bearish, or ranging structure interpretation wrong.

title: Avoid over-labeling structure
description: Make sure you are not marking every small fluctuation as a new structural high or low.
advice: Use meaningful swings and consistent rules. Too many labels can make a simple market structure appear unnecessarily complicated.

title: Finalize the structural direction
description: Summarize the current structure as bullish, bearish, ranging, or unclear.
advice: Write down the main structural evidence and the level that would invalidate your conclusion before moving to key areas.

title: Mark major support
description: Identify price areas where buyers have previously shown strong interest or where price reacted upward.
advice: Prioritize areas with multiple meaningful reactions rather than marking every small bounce as support.

title: Mark major resistance
description: Identify price areas where sellers have previously shown strong interest or where price reacted downward.
advice: Focus on significant rejection zones and repeated reactions.

title: Mark higher-timeframe levels
description: Identify important support and resistance areas from Daily, 4H, and Weekly charts.
advice: Higher-timeframe levels generally deserve more attention than minor intraday levels.

title: Mark previous day high
description: Identify the previous trading day's high as a potential reaction and liquidity area.
advice: Watch how price behaves when approaching or sweeping the previous day's high.

title: Mark previous day low
description: Identify the previous trading day's low as a potential reaction and liquidity area.
advice: Watch for rejection, breakout, or liquidity sweep behavior around the level.

title: Mark previous week high
description: Identify the previous week's high as a higher-timeframe reference point.
advice: Previous-week extremes can attract liquidity and produce meaningful reactions.

title: Mark previous week low
description: Identify the previous week's low as a higher-timeframe reference point.
advice: Use it as context for potential liquidity, rejection, or continuation.

title: Mark previous month high
description: Identify the previous month's high as a major higher-timeframe reference.
advice: Monthly extremes can be particularly important when price approaches them after a prolonged move.

title: Mark previous month low
description: Identify the previous month's low as a major higher-timeframe reference.
advice: Consider the level in relation to the current monthly and weekly structure.

title: Identify supply zones
description: Find areas where strong selling previously caused price to move away aggressively.
advice: Look for zones associated with meaningful displacement rather than every bearish candle.

title: Identify demand zones
description: Find areas where strong buying previously caused price to move away aggressively.
advice: Focus on zones that produced significant upward displacement.

title: Identify Order Blocks
description: Mark potential institutional order-block areas according to your trading methodology.
advice: Use order blocks in combination with structure, displacement, liquidity, and location rather than treating every candle as an order block.

title: Identify Fair Value Gaps
description: Look for three-candle price imbalances created by strong directional movement.
advice: Give greater importance to FVGs that appear with strong displacement and align with the broader market structure.

title: Check liquidity above highs
description: Identify obvious highs where stop orders and breakout orders may be concentrated.
advice: Equal highs, previous highs, and obvious swing highs can become important liquidity areas.

title: Check liquidity below lows
description: Identify obvious lows where stop orders and breakout orders may be concentrated.
advice: Equal lows, previous lows, and obvious swing lows can become important liquidity areas.

title: Check equal highs
description: Identify multiple highs forming around approximately the same price.
advice: Treat equal highs as potential liquidity rather than assuming they will automatically be broken.

title: Check equal lows
description: Identify multiple lows forming around approximately the same price.
advice: Treat equal lows as potential liquidity rather than assuming they will automatically be broken.

title: Mark psychological levels
description: Identify important round-number price levels that traders may pay attention to.
advice: Examples include major whole numbers and half numbers. Use them as supporting context, not automatic entry levels.

title: Check Fibonacci retracement levels
description: Use Fibonacci retracement to identify potential reaction areas within a meaningful price swing.
advice: Draw Fibonacci from a clearly defined swing and combine it with structure or other key areas.

title: Check Fibonacci confluence
description: Determine whether Fibonacci levels overlap with existing support, resistance, or other important areas.
advice: A Fibonacci level becomes more interesting when it aligns with independent structural evidence.

title: Mark session highs and lows
description: Identify important highs and lows created during major trading sessions.
advice: London and New York session extremes can become useful intraday reference points.

title: Mark Asian session range
description: Identify the high and low of the Asian trading session when using session-based strategies.
advice: The range can provide useful context for later London or New York price movement.

title: Check opening prices
description: Mark relevant daily, weekly, or session opening prices.
advice: Opening levels can provide useful reference points for understanding whether price is trading above or below an important period's open.

title: Check market gaps
description: Identify significant gaps between one trading period's close and the next period's open.
advice: Determine whether the gap is meaningful in the context of the instrument and timeframe rather than assuming every small gap matters.

title: Identify consolidation zones
description: Mark areas where price spent significant time moving sideways before expanding.
advice: Previous consolidation areas can become important reaction or decision zones when price returns.

title: Identify breakout levels
description: Mark important boundaries where price may break out of an established range or structure.
advice: Wait for actual price behavior around the level instead of assuming that a breakout will happen.

title: Check reclaimed levels
description: Identify levels that price previously broke and later recovered or reclaimed.
advice: A reclaimed level can sometimes change from resistance into support or support into resistance.

title: Check broken support and resistance
description: Identify important levels that have recently been broken.
advice: Observe whether the broken level is accepted beyond or quickly rejected back into the previous range.

title: Check price location within the range
description: Determine whether price is near the upper, middle, or lower portion of its current meaningful range.
advice: Location helps determine whether chasing a move is sensible or whether price is approaching an area where reaction is more likely.

title: Find confluence between key areas
description: Look for multiple independent technical factors overlapping around the same price region.
advice: Examples include support plus Fibonacci, liquidity plus resistance, or an order block plus FVG. More confluence can increase interest but does not guarantee a reaction.

title: Separate strong and weak levels
description: Rank the marked areas according to their importance and supporting evidence.
advice: Prioritize higher-timeframe levels, strong displacement origins, repeated reactions, and areas supported by multiple independent factors.

title: Avoid marking too many levels
description: Remove unnecessary zones so the chart remains readable and decision-making stays focused.
advice: If every price level is marked as important, none of them are truly important. Keep only the areas relevant to the current trade idea.

title: Check distance to the nearest key area
description: Determine how much room price has before reaching the next important support, resistance, or liquidity area.
advice: Avoid taking trades directly into nearby opposing key areas when there is insufficient room for the setup to develop.

title: Determine the reaction area
description: Identify the specific zone where you would expect price to potentially react if your directional idea is correct.
advice: Define the area before looking for an entry trigger so you are not chasing price after it has already moved.

title: Define invalidation around the key area
description: Determine what price action would invalidate the importance of your selected area.
advice: Know what would make you stop treating the zone as valid before price reaches it.

title: Identify the target area
description: Determine the next meaningful area price could potentially move toward if the setup succeeds.
advice: Potential targets can include liquidity, previous highs or lows, support, resistance, or other significant market areas.

title: Confirm key areas across timeframes
description: Check whether an important area remains relevant when viewed across multiple timeframes.
advice: A level that appears on several meaningful timeframes can provide stronger context than a level visible only on a very low timeframe.

title: Finalize the key areas
description: Reduce the chart to the most relevant support, resistance, liquidity, imbalance, and other important areas.
advice: Before moving to trend confirmation, know where price is coming from, where it is now, and which areas could cause the next meaningful reaction.

title: Identify the current trend
description: Determine whether the market is trending upward, trending downward, or moving sideways.
advice: Start with the higher timeframe and identify the overall direction from the sequence of highs and lows.

title: Confirm higher highs and higher lows
description: Confirm that bullish price action is producing a sequence of higher highs and higher lows.
advice: Look for consistent bullish structure rather than calling the market bullish from a single upward move.

title: Confirm lower highs and lower lows
description: Confirm that bearish price action is producing a sequence of lower highs and lower lows.
advice: Look for repeated bearish structure rather than assuming every downward move represents a downtrend.

title: Check for a ranging market
description: Determine whether price is moving sideways between relatively clear support and resistance areas.
advice: If price repeatedly fails to establish new highs or lows, treat the market as ranging until structure clearly changes.

title: Check the higher timeframe trend
description: Identify the broader trend before relying on a lower-timeframe setup.
advice: Understand the higher-timeframe direction first, then determine whether your trading timeframe agrees with it.

title: Check the trading timeframe trend
description: Confirm that the trend is present on the timeframe you are actually using for the setup.
advice: Do not force a higher-timeframe trend onto a lower timeframe that is currently moving in the opposite direction.

title: Check trend strength
description: Determine whether the current trend is moving with strong momentum or beginning to weaken.
advice: Compare impulsive moves with pullbacks. Strong continuation with controlled pullbacks generally provides stronger trend conditions.

title: Check pullback quality
description: Analyze how price behaves when it temporarily moves against the current trend.
advice: Healthy trends often produce controlled pullbacks followed by continuation. Deep or aggressive pullbacks can indicate weakening momentum.

title: Check EMA direction
description: Use the direction and slope of your selected EMA or EMAs as supporting trend information.
advice: A clearly sloping EMA can support the trend direction, while a flat EMA often suggests weaker or ranging conditions.

title: Check EMA alignment
description: Determine whether multiple EMAs are aligned in the same direction.
advice: Aligned EMAs can support a directional trend, while tangled or repeatedly crossing EMAs can indicate uncertainty.

title: Check price reaction around the EMA
description: Observe whether price is consistently respecting the EMA during pullbacks.
advice: Repeated reactions around an EMA can support the trend thesis, but use price structure as the primary confirmation.

title: Check momentum
description: Determine whether momentum is supporting the current directional movement.
advice: Compare the strength and speed of recent impulses with previous moves to identify strengthening or weakening momentum.

title: Check for trend exhaustion
description: Look for signs that the existing trend may be losing strength.
advice: Watch for weaker continuation, increasingly deep pullbacks, failed breakouts, and repeated rejection around important areas.

title: Check for timeframe conflict
description: Identify whether higher and lower timeframes are showing conflicting directional conditions.
advice: When timeframes strongly disagree, reduce confidence and wait for clearer alignment rather than forcing a trade.

title: Check breakout continuation
description: Determine whether price continues in the breakout direction after breaking an important high, low, or range.
advice: A breakout followed by sustained continuation is more convincing than a breakout that immediately returns inside the previous structure.

title: Check for a false breakout
description: Determine whether price briefly breaks a level before quickly returning through it.
advice: A failed breakout can signal rejection and potential change in short-term direction, so do not assume every breakout will continue.

title: Finalize trend confirmation
description: Reduce the trend analysis to one clear directional condition: bullish, bearish, ranging, or unclear.
advice: Only move to entry confirmation when structure, momentum, timeframe context, and trend behavior provide a sufficiently clear picture.

title: Wait for price to reach the key area
description: Confirm that price has reached the support, resistance, liquidity, imbalance, or other area identified during analysis.
advice: Do not look for an entry in the middle of nowhere. Let price come to your planned area first.

title: Check the reaction at the key area
description: Observe how price behaves when it reaches the area of interest.
advice: Look for rejection, acceptance, displacement, consolidation, or other meaningful price behavior before considering an entry.

title: Wait for confirmation
description: Require your predefined entry confirmation instead of entering simply because price touched your level.
advice: Define what confirmation means for your strategy before the trade. Avoid changing the requirement after price reaches the area.

title: Check for rejection
description: Determine whether price is being rejected from the area in the direction of your trade idea.
advice: Look for meaningful rejection rather than treating every wick or small candle as confirmation.

title: Check for displacement
description: Look for a strong and decisive price movement away from the key area.
advice: Strong displacement can provide evidence that one side of the market has gained control, especially when it aligns with your existing bias.

title: Check for a structure shift
description: Determine whether short-term market structure has changed in the expected direction.
advice: Use a meaningful break or shift in structure as confirmation rather than relying on a single candle.

title: Check candle confirmation
description: Evaluate whether the candle behavior supports the intended direction at the entry area.
advice: Consider engulfing candles, rejection candles, strong closes, and other patterns that are actually part of your strategy.

title: Check momentum confirmation
description: Confirm that momentum is supporting the intended direction at the time of entry.
advice: Avoid entering when price is showing weak or conflicting momentum unless your strategy specifically targets that condition.

title: Check volume confirmation
description: Use volume information when it is relevant to your market and strategy.
advice: Look for volume behavior that supports your interpretation of the move, but do not treat volume alone as an entry signal.

title: Check breakout and retest
description: Determine whether price has broken an important level and successfully retested it.
advice: A clean breakout followed by a controlled retest can provide stronger confirmation than entering immediately on the first breakout candle.

title: Check liquidity sweep
description: Determine whether price has taken liquidity around a previous high, low, or obvious level before reversing.
advice: A liquidity sweep becomes more meaningful when the reaction afterward aligns with your structure and directional bias.

title: Check for confirmation from multiple factors
description: Determine whether more than one independent confirmation supports the trade idea.
advice: Prefer confluence between structure, key areas, price action, momentum, and other valid factors rather than relying on one signal.

title: Check entry timeframe
description: Confirm that the entry signal is valid on the timeframe you use for execution.
advice: Use the higher timeframe for context and the execution timeframe for precise confirmation. Do not confuse the two.

title: Check if the setup is already invalid
description: Determine whether price has already moved too far or violated the conditions required for your setup.
advice: If the original setup is gone, accept it and wait for another opportunity instead of forcing an entry.

title: Check entry quality
description: Evaluate whether the confirmation provides a clean and logical entry rather than a late or emotional entry.
advice: Avoid chasing price after a large move. A valid setup can still become a poor entry if the risk-to-reward relationship has deteriorated.

title: Check invalidation before entering
description: Know exactly what price behavior would prove the trade idea wrong.
advice: Define your invalidation point before clicking buy or sell. If you cannot explain where the idea becomes invalid, the setup is not ready.

title: Finalize the entry confirmation
description: Confirm that the planned area, market structure, price reaction, momentum, and entry trigger all agree with the trade idea.
advice: Only proceed when your predefined confirmation rules are satisfied. If confirmation is missing, waiting is the correct action.

title: Identify the dominant chart pattern
description: Look for clear price patterns such as triangles, flags, wedges, channels, double tops, double bottoms, and other recognizable formations.
advice: Only consider patterns that are clearly visible and properly formed. A pattern should support the broader market structure rather than being forced onto random price movement.

title: Check the pattern location
description: Determine where the pattern is forming relative to support, resistance, liquidity, trend, and other key areas.
advice: A pattern forming at a meaningful location is generally more useful than the same pattern appearing in the middle of nowhere.

title: Check the pattern structure
description: Make sure the pattern has clear boundaries, recognizable swing points, and logical price behavior.
advice: If you need to heavily manipulate trendlines or ignore several price swings to make the pattern fit, the pattern may not be reliable.

title: Check for a breakout or rejection
description: Observe whether price breaks the pattern, rejects its boundary, or continues to consolidate inside it.
advice: Wait for price to show what it is actually doing instead of assuming the pattern will resolve in a particular direction.

title: Check for confirmation
description: Look for supporting evidence such as a strong close, market-structure shift, momentum, volume, or reaction from a key area.
advice: Use pattern recognition as one part of the setup. Stronger trades usually have multiple pieces of evidence pointing in the same direction.

title: Check for false breakouts
description: Determine whether price has briefly moved beyond a pattern boundary but failed to continue.
advice: A breakout is not confirmed simply because price crosses a trendline or level. Watch how price closes and behaves afterward.

title: Check volume when available
description: Use volume to evaluate whether a breakout or major price movement is supported by increased participation.
advice: Volume can provide useful confirmation, but it should not override price structure or your broader trading plan.

title: Check multiple timeframes
description: Compare the pattern with the higher-timeframe and lower-timeframe price structure.
advice: A pattern on a lower timeframe can be less meaningful if it directly conflicts with a strong higher-timeframe structure.

title: Check the expected pattern target
description: Estimate where price could reasonably travel if the pattern completes successfully.
advice: A pattern is more useful when its potential movement provides enough room for a logical trade relative to your risk.

title: Check the invalidation point
description: Identify the price level or behavior that would prove the pattern is no longer valid.
advice: Know exactly what would invalidate the pattern before entering. If there is no clear invalidation point, the setup may not be well defined.

title: Avoid forcing patterns
description: Make sure the pattern is obvious enough that another trader could reasonably identify the same structure.
advice: If you have to convince yourself that a pattern exists, treat it as weak or ignore it.

title: Check whether the pattern supports the trade idea
description: Compare the pattern direction with your market bias, structure, key areas, and planned entry.
advice: The pattern should add confluence to the setup rather than being the only reason for taking the trade.

title: Confirm multiple factors agree
description: Check whether several independent pieces of analysis support the same trade direction.
advice: Look for agreement between market bias, structure, key areas, trend, entry confirmation, and other relevant factors instead of relying on one signal.

title: Check higher-timeframe alignment
description: Compare the current setup with the direction and structure visible on higher timeframes.
advice: A setup generally becomes more meaningful when the lower-timeframe opportunity makes sense within the higher-timeframe context.

title: Check market structure alignment
description: Determine whether BOS, CHoCH, swing highs, swing lows, and other structural information support the trade.
advice: Don't treat a single structure break as enough confirmation. Consider the surrounding price action and overall structure.

title: Check key-area confluence
description: Determine whether the setup is occurring at an important support, resistance, supply, demand, liquidity, order block, or imbalance area.
advice: A technical signal occurring at a meaningful location is generally more useful than the same signal appearing in an arbitrary area.

title: Check trend alignment
description: Compare the trade direction with the current trend and momentum.
advice: When trading with the trend, look for entries that allow you to participate in the existing directional movement rather than fighting it without a strong reason.

title: Check price-action confirmation
description: Look for rejection, engulfing candles, displacement, breakouts, retests, or other meaningful price-action behavior.
advice: Use price action to confirm that buyers or sellers are actually responding at the area you identified.

title: Check liquidity conditions
description: Consider whether liquidity has been taken, is resting near the setup, or could influence the next price movement.
advice: Understand where obvious stops and liquidity may be located before assuming price will move directly toward your target.

title: Check Fibonacci confluence
description: Use Fibonacci retracement or extension levels to determine whether they overlap with important technical areas.
advice: Fibonacci becomes more useful when its levels overlap with structure, support/resistance, or other meaningful areas.

title: Check volume confluence
description: Use volume to evaluate whether important price movements or breakouts have meaningful participation behind them.
advice: Volume can strengthen a setup when it agrees with price action, but it should not be treated as a standalone signal.

title: Check indicator agreement
description: If indicators are part of your strategy, determine whether EMA, RSI, MACD, or other tools support the price-action analysis.
advice: Use indicators as supporting evidence rather than stacking many indicators that measure essentially the same thing.

title: Check session confluence
description: Consider whether the setup is forming during a session or session overlap that normally provides suitable liquidity and activity for your strategy.
advice: A setup can behave differently depending on when it forms. Consider session conditions before giving the setup additional weight.

title: Check macro alignment
description: Compare the technical setup with important news, economic conditions, DXY, Gold, and broader market sentiment when relevant.
advice: Macro information should provide context and risk awareness rather than forcing a technical trade in one direction.

title: Check for conflicting signals
description: Look for evidence that contradicts your trade idea before entering.
advice: Don't only search for reasons to enter. Actively look for reasons why the setup could fail.

title: Avoid counting the same signal twice
description: Determine whether your confluences are genuinely independent or simply different ways of describing the same market condition.
advice: Five indicators pointing in the same direction do not necessarily provide five independent confirmations.

title: Check overall setup quality
description: Combine the strongest evidence and decide whether the setup is clear, mixed, or weak.
advice: Good confluence should make the trade idea clearer. If adding more analysis only makes the decision more confusing, step back and reassess.

title: Define the maximum risk
description: Decide how much of your account you are willing to lose if the trade reaches its invalidation point.
advice: Set the risk before calculating your position size. Keep the amount small enough that one losing trade does not significantly affect your ability to continue trading.

title: Set the stop-loss level
description: Identify the price level where your trade idea becomes invalid.
advice: Place the stop based on market structure and trade invalidation rather than choosing an arbitrary distance from the entry.

title: Calculate position size
description: Determine the appropriate position size using your account balance, risk amount, entry price, and stop-loss distance.
advice: Calculate position size after defining your stop and maximum risk. Do not increase the position simply because the setup looks highly confident.

title: Check risk-to-reward
description: Compare the amount you could lose with the realistic amount you could potentially gain.
advice: Make sure the potential reward justifies the risk and that your target is supported by actual market structure rather than an arbitrary ratio.

title: Define the profit target
description: Determine where you expect the trade idea to reach a meaningful objective.
advice: Use key areas, liquidity, structure, or other logical price objectives when selecting your target.

title: Check stop-loss placement
description: Make sure your stop is positioned beyond the level that would genuinely invalidate your setup.
advice: Avoid placing stops so close that normal market noise can remove you from a valid setup, but don't widen the stop simply to avoid taking a loss.

title: Check spread and trading costs
description: Consider spread, commission, swaps, and other trading costs before entering.
advice: Make sure transaction costs are reasonable relative to the expected movement of the trade, especially when using tight stops or short-term strategies.

title: Check news risk
description: Determine whether upcoming economic events could create abnormal volatility or slippage.
advice: Know whether major news is approaching and decide in advance whether your strategy allows holding the position through it.

title: Check correlation risk
description: Identify whether multiple open trades are exposed to the same currency, index, commodity, or market factor.
advice: Several positions that look different can still represent one large directional bet if they are strongly correlated.

title: Check total account exposure
description: Review all current positions and pending orders before opening another trade.
advice: Consider your combined exposure instead of evaluating every trade independently.

title: Define the invalidation condition
description: Clearly identify what must happen for your original trade thesis to become wrong.
advice: Know your invalidation before entering. Once the thesis is invalidated, don't move the stop simply because you want the trade to survive.

title: Plan the trade before entering
description: Define entry, stop-loss, target, position size, and maximum risk before executing the trade.
advice: A complete plan reduces emotional decisions after the position is already open.

title: Define the maximum daily loss
description: Set a personal limit for how much you are willing to lose during one trading day.
advice: Once your daily loss limit is reached, stop trading and review your decisions instead of trying to recover the loss immediately.

title: Check for revenge trading
description: Determine whether the current trade is being taken because of a previous loss or emotional reaction.
advice: A new trade should have its own independent setup and risk plan. Previous losses should not determine the size or direction of the next trade.

title: Check whether the trade is worth taking
description: Evaluate the setup, risk, reward, market conditions, and potential invalidation together.
advice: If the risk is unclear, the target is unrealistic, or the position size is uncomfortable, skipping the trade is a valid risk-management decision.

title: Check my emotional state
description: Assess whether you are calm, focused, and able to follow your trading plan objectively.
advice: Trade when you are mentally prepared to accept either outcome. If you feel angry, anxious, excited, or desperate to make money, step away before entering.

title: Check for fear of missing out
description: Determine whether you want to enter because the setup is valid or because price is moving quickly without you.
advice: A missed trade is better than a forced trade. Wait for your planned conditions instead of chasing price.

title: Check for revenge trading
description: Make sure the trade is not an attempt to recover a previous loss quickly.
advice: Treat every trade as a new decision. Never increase risk simply because the previous trade lost.

title: Check for overconfidence
description: Assess whether recent winning trades are making you more aggressive or careless.
advice: A winning streak does not guarantee that the next trade will win. Keep the same rules and risk management regardless of recent results.

title: Accept the possibility of loss
description: Accept that even a high-quality setup can fail.
advice: Before entering, mentally accept the planned loss. If the potential loss feels unacceptable, reduce the risk or skip the trade.

title: Check whether I am forcing the setup
description: Determine whether you are searching for reasons to enter after already deciding that you want the trade.
advice: Analyze the chart objectively. If the setup is not clear, don't manufacture confluence just to justify an entry.

title: Check my attachment to the trade
description: Make sure you are willing to exit if the original trade idea becomes invalid.
advice: Your position should never become more important than your trading plan. Be prepared to accept that your analysis can be wrong.

title: Check for impatience
description: Determine whether you are entering because you are tired of waiting for your setup.
advice: The market does not owe you a trade. Wait for your conditions instead of lowering your standards because nothing has happened yet.

title: Check for hesitation
description: Determine whether fear is preventing you from taking a valid setup that meets your predefined rules.
advice: If the setup meets your plan and the risk is acceptable, execute according to your system rather than trying to guarantee the outcome.

title: Check for impulsive trading
description: Make sure the trade was planned rather than triggered by a sudden candle, headline, social-media post, or emotional reaction.
advice: Pause before entering and run through your checklist. If you cannot explain why the trade qualifies, don't take it.

title: Check my need to be right
description: Separate being correct about the market from following a profitable trading process.
advice: Your job is not to prove your prediction correct. Your job is to manage risk and respond to what price actually does.

title: Check whether I am moving my rules
description: Identify whether you are changing your entry, stop, target, or risk rules simply because the trade is not behaving as expected.
advice: Do not rewrite your plan after entering just to avoid taking the planned loss.

title: Check my trading frequency
description: Review whether you are taking more trades than your strategy normally produces.
advice: More trades do not automatically mean more opportunities. Avoid entering marginal setups simply because you want to stay active.

title: Check my focus
description: Make sure you can actively monitor and manage the trade without unnecessary distractions.
advice: Avoid trading when you are distracted, exhausted, rushed, or unable to follow your planned management rules.

title: Accept that no trade is also a decision
description: Recognize that staying out is a valid outcome when the setup does not meet your conditions.
advice: You do not need to participate in every market movement. Protecting your capital and waiting for a better opportunity is part of the process.

title: Confirm the market bias
description: Make sure the overall directional bias is clear and supported by your analysis.
advice: You should be able to explain why you favor bullish, bearish, or neutral conditions without relying on a single signal.

title: Confirm the market structure
description: Verify that the current structure supports the trade direction and that there is no major structural conflict.
advice: Identify the important swing points and know what price action would invalidate your structural thesis.

title: Confirm the key area
description: Make sure the planned entry is occurring at a meaningful support, resistance, liquidity, supply, demand, or other key area.
advice: Avoid entering simply because price is moving. Know why the current location matters.

title: Confirm the trend
description: Check whether the current trend and momentum support your intended direction.
advice: If you are trading against the dominant trend, require stronger evidence and a clear reason for doing so.

title: Confirm the entry trigger
description: Make sure the specific condition required by your strategy has actually occurred.
advice: Do not enter simply because the price has reached your area. Wait for your predefined entry confirmation.

title: Confirm the confluence
description: Review whether multiple independent factors support the same trade idea.
advice: Strong confluence should make the setup clearer. Avoid counting several indicators that are essentially measuring the same thing as separate confirmations.

title: Check for conflicting information
description: Actively search for evidence that contradicts your trade idea.
advice: Do not only look for reasons to enter. Ask yourself what could make this trade fail before committing capital.

title: Check the news environment
description: Review upcoming economic events and determine whether news could interfere with the setup.
advice: If major news is approaching, decide whether your strategy supports trading before or through the event.

title: Confirm the stop-loss
description: Identify the exact level where the trade thesis becomes invalid.
advice: Your stop should have a logical reason based on the setup. Never enter without knowing where you are wrong.

title: Confirm the take-profit
description: Identify a realistic target based on structure, liquidity, key areas, or other logical market objectives.
advice: Do not choose a target only because it produces an attractive risk-to-reward ratio. The market should provide a reasonable path toward it.

title: Confirm the risk-to-reward
description: Compare the planned risk with the realistic potential reward of the setup.
advice: If the potential reward does not justify the risk, skip the trade rather than forcing the setup.

title: Confirm the position size
description: Make sure the position size matches your predefined account risk and stop-loss distance.
advice: Calculate position size from risk first. Do not increase your position because you feel especially confident about the setup.

title: Check my psychological state
description: Make sure you are calm enough to execute and manage the trade according to your plan.
advice: If you are experiencing FOMO, revenge trading, fear, greed, or a strong need to recover losses, do not force the trade.

title: Ask whether I am forcing the trade
description: Take a final step back and determine whether the setup genuinely meets your rules.
advice: If you need to make excuses, reinterpret your rules, or search aggressively for additional confirmation, the setup may not be ready.

title: Define the exact trade plan
description: Write down the entry, stop-loss, take-profit, position size, risk, and invalidation condition before execution.
advice: If you cannot clearly describe the trade before entering, you probably do not have a complete setup.

title: Make the final decision
description: After completing the analysis, choose one clear action: buy, sell, or no trade.
advice: Do not create a trade simply because the checklist is complete. The final decision should be based on the quality of the complete setup. No trade is a valid decision.
